category_feedback.specific_evidence: expanded_walkthrough.rationale names a real trap ('child sees bar at height 4 on a scaled graph (1 unit = 5) and says 4 children instead of 20') and recovery_moves are concrete ('Use scale check card', 'Drill scale x bar = count', 'Compare scaled vs 1-to-1'), but no research is cited and recovery does not branch by what the diagnostic told you about the child.
category_feedback.required_fix: Anchor the scale-blind trap to research on graph comprehension (e.g., Friel, Curcio & Bright 2001 'elementary/intermediate/overall' levels of graph reading; Shaughnessy on data analysis). Then BRANCH recovery_moves: if child reads y-axis numbers fluently but ignores them, drill 'point-to-axis-first' before reading any bar; if child cannot decode the y-axis labels at all (e.g., misreads 0,5,10,15 as 1,2,3,4), drop back to skip-counting by 5s on a number line before returning to the graph; if child reads scale correctly but multiplies wrong, isolate the multiplication fact (4 x 5) on a separate card. State each branch with the diagnostic signal that triggers it.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: consolidation.activity_name = 'Detective Dot's Scale Brag' and exit_routine = "Each child writes one scale: 'My scale is 1 unit = ___.'" Detective Dot anchors minds_on/action/consolidation and success_criteria all use 'I can', but there is no distinctive quotable refrain or chant carrying between lessons — 'Detective Dot says — pick scale to FIT the grid' is teacher narration, not a child-chantable refrain.
category_feedback.required_fix: Give Detective Dot a memorable scale-themed chant that the class echoes back at the close of every minds_on AND consolidation, e.g., 'Read the SCALE first, then read the BAR — bar times scale shows how MANY there are!' Add it to teacher_script (children echo on cue) and to consolidation.exit_routine so children carry it into Lessons 4 and 5. Quote the chant verbatim in at least two places in the lesson so the recurring character has a refrain children remember two months later.

category_feedback.specific_evidence: Conceptual progression is explicit (one-to-one would need bars 30/15/10/5 -> too tall; many-to-one with 1 unit = 5 -> 6/3/2/1) and 'scale x bar = count' is named precisely, but children do not invent or compare strategies — scales are handed to them ('Pick scale: 1 unit = 5 children', Station B 'scale = 5'). No research-grounded misconception framing (Friel/Curcio/Bright on graph comprehension, or Shaughnessy on data sense).
category_feedback.required_fix: In action.steps, restructure Station C so children INVENT and COMPARE scales for the same data set (e.g., 50-student data: have one pair try scale=2, another scale=5, another scale=10) and then debrief which fits the grid best and WHY — making the 'fits-the-grid' criterion the children's discovery rather than the teacher's rule. Then in expanded_walkthrough.rationale, name the misconception in research-grounded terms (cite Friel, Curcio & Bright 2001 levels of graph reading, or Shaughnessy on transnumeration) so the trap is anchored to the literature.
